lead.headline: Nevada's data center boom could need about 34,000 acre-feet of water a year, most of it at power plants
lead.dek: An updated Desert Research Institute study puts direct cooling demand near 12,800 acre-feet a year by 2036. The water consumed to generate their electricity is far larger.
body: The Desert Research Institute has revised its January estimate of what data centers will mean for water in Nevada, the driest state. The update uses NV Energy's 2026 planning forecast, which lists 39 proposed high load data centers requesting 16,530 megawatts by 2036. The January study covered 12 projects and about 5,900 megawatts.

At the midpoint of its scenarios, the institute estimates direct cooling use of about 12,770 acre-feet a year, roughly 4 billion gallons, plus about 21,283 acre-feet consumed at the utility level to generate the power. Data centers are about 5% of NV Energy's sales today and are expected to reach 64% by 2046, according to the Nevada Independent.

The supply question is where the business case sits. The report says new growth will largely come from unappropriated groundwater, water reclamation or water transfers, and that direct demand will depend on cooling technology, with direct to chip and immersion systems among the more efficient options. A closed loop 100 megawatt facility in Las Vegas used less than 2 acre-feet in 2025, while an evaporative Google site in Henderson used about 636 acre-feet in 2024.

pipe.source: New demand will lean on unappropriated groundwater, reclaimed water and transfers in a state with little surface water to spare.
pipe.treat: Reclaimed and brackish sources mean more treatment ahead of cooling systems and more brine to manage.
pipe.use: Cooling design decides direct use: closed loop sites can use almost nothing, evaporative sites hundreds of acre-feet.
pipe.reuse: Reclamation is one of the three named supply routes, which puts municipal effluent in play as an industrial asset.
pipe.discharge: Blowdown from evaporative cooling concentrates salts and has to go somewhere in a closed desert basin.

use.text: Grid water now outweighs cooling water. Power siting is a water risk, not just an energy one.
Reclaimed water contracts with data center developers can become a revenue line.
Closed loop and direct to chip cooling shrink the permit fight in arid states.
Brackish treatment, reuse and low water cooling are the products Nevada buyers will need.

briefs.headline: California Water Service becomes Watermark Utilities and heads for Nevada and Oregon
briefs.text: California Water Service Group will trade under the name Watermark Utilities from November 30, keeping the CWT ticker, according to an 8-K filed November 18. The company, which serves more than 2.2 million people through subsidiaries in California, Hawaii, New Mexico, Texas and Washington, says it plans to expand into Nevada and Oregon before year end.
briefs.why: A new name that drops the home state signals a multi-state acquirer. It arrives as American Water and Essential pursue their merger and small system purchases keep the consolidation pipeline full.

briefs.headline: Saudi Water Authority cancels WABAG's $272 million Yanbu desalination award
briefs.text: The Saudi Water Authority cancelled the tender for a 300 million liter a day seawater reverse osmosis plant at Yanbu, citing internal reasons, VA Tech Wabag told Indian exchanges on November 14. WABAG had signed the contract awarded in July 2025 and sent it for counter-signature, which never came. It was the second award of the project to the company, after one in September 2024 at about $317 million.
briefs.why: Gulf desalination awards are not final until the buyer signs. Contractors carrying Saudi projects in their order books may face closer questions from investors. The authority has not said whether it will re-tender.

briefs.headline: Texas regulators hold off on Aqua Texas rates and weigh a five-year phase-in
briefs.text: The Public Utility Commission of Texas ended a November 19 hearing on Aqua Texas rates without a decision. Commissioners questioned the utility's records and asked staff to calculate rates under the administrative law judges' recommendations. Options include lower rates on those recommendations, a five-year phase-in that staff had proposed, or sending the case back for more review. Aqua Texas says its recordkeeping has improved.
briefs.why: Rate shock is becoming a political limit on how fast investor-owned utilities recover capital spending. A ruling could come at an open meeting as soon as December.

briefs.headline: Select Water closes its $700 million purchase of Pilot Water Solutions
briefs.text: Select Water Solutions completed its acquisition of Delaware Basin produced water company Pilot Water Solutions on November 2, paying about $600 million in cash and 5.1 million shares. Pilot brings about 2.7 million barrels a day of active permitted disposal capacity and more than 700 miles of pipeline. Select funded the deal with $900 million of 7.625% senior notes due 2034.
briefs.why: Produced water is now a midstream business financed like one. Select expects the combined company to handle more than 2.5 million barrels a day in 2027.

briefs.headline: TasWater's new sewer pricing cuts hospital charges about 70% while some customers faced 500% rises
briefs.text: Tasmania's water utility moved some non-residential fixed sewerage charges to a basis of water connection size from July 1. Health department documents show Launceston General Hospital's fixed charge fell to $12,531 for July to September from $67,361 a year earlier. Customers with large connections, such as sports grounds, were initially set for increases of up to 500%, and TasWater paused those bills on October 2. The utility says it still expects to collect its planned revenue.
briefs.why: Tariff redesign shifts who pays without changing what a utility collects. Utilities moving to capacity based charges should model the outliers before bills go out.

company.name: Xylem
company.headline: Xylem is shrinking to grow
company.body: Third quarter results on October 27 missed revenue expectations as utility project timing slipped. Management answered with portfolio moves: it intends to divest Applied Water International and Specialty Flow Control and will report three segments instead of four from 2027. In July it agreed to buy WaterFleet from EagleTree Capital for about $200 million, adding to its industrial water platform.

leader.name: Estelle Brachlianoff
leader.body: Brachlianoff has run Veolia since July 2022, and shareholders renewed her board seat in April 2026 through the 2030 annual meeting. Her GreenUp plan leans on water technology and hazardous waste: Veolia agreed to buy US hazardous waste company Clean Earth for about $3 billion, won two Mumbai water projects in February and launched an integrated offer for data centers.

supplier.name: Ecolab
supplier.headline: Ecolab's water business is being pulled by chips and AI data centers
body: Ecolab reported third quarter sales up 13% to $4.69 billion on October 27, with organic growth accelerating to 7%. Chairman and chief executive Christophe Beck called the quarter an inflection point, and the water segment is where the change shows most clearly.

Global Water sales rose 20% at fixed currency to $2.48 billion. Eleven points came from the Ovivo Electronics and CoolIT acquisitions, and the rest from organic growth led by Global High-Tech, which grew 63% organically on semiconductor and data center demand.

The cost of that bet is visible too. CoolIT amortization and financing took roughly 10% off adjusted earnings growth, holding adjusted EPS to $2.18, up 5%. Management guides full-year adjusted EPS to $8.10 to $8.20.
supplier.why: Fabs and hyperscale data centers now set the pace for industrial water treatment. Expect bundled water, cooling and digital contracts and tighter supply of ultrapure water expertise.

innovation.name: Claros Technologies
innovation.headline: Claros takes PFAS destruction to full scale at Daikin
innovation.body: Most PFAS treatment moves the chemicals into another waste stream. Claros breaks them apart with its ClarosTechUV system. On October 1 it signed a commercial agreement with Daikin America for full-scale deployment at Daikin's plant in Decatur, Alabama, after a December 2025 run treated more than 170,000 gallons of process water with greater than 99.99% destruction of target PFAS.

investor.name: Burnt Island Ventures
investor.headline: The most active water-only venture firm
investor.body: Founded in New York by water industry veteran Tom Ferguson, Burnt Island invests only in early stage water technology. Xylem anchored both of its funds, with climate fund of funds WovenEarth Ventures joining Fund II. Published deal trackers show 2026 investments in Aquatic Labs, Crew Carbon, Biota and Verdi.

capital.intro: Private equity has executed 435 water deals across 25 countries since 2015 and more than doubled its holdings since 2019, according to Bluefield Research. Most of those assets are under three years old, which points to an exit wave.

security.headline: The UN says the world has entered water bankruptcy
security.text: A UN University report in January argued that groundwater depletion, overallocation and pollution have pushed many basins past the point of recovery, and that "crisis" no longer describes it.

security.text: The two countries signed a formal agreement in September on new operating guidelines for the river that supplies seven US states and northern Mexico.

security.headline: The Gulf runs on desalination

place.name: Marina Barrage
place.headline: A dam in the middle of a city that people come to picnic on
body: Marina Barrage closes the 350 meter wide Marina Channel with nine steel crest gates, keeping seawater out and turning the bay into Singapore's 15th reservoir and the first in the city center. Its catchment of about 10,000 hectares is the largest in the country, and the same structure protects low lying downtown streets from flooding.

The pump house is topped by a grass roof of about 11,000 square meters, open around the clock, where people fly kites, picnic and watch the skyline beside a solar installation. National water agency PUB counted close to 15 million visitors in the barrage's first ten years.
place.visit: Free shuttle bus from Marina Bay MRT station. The green roof and public areas are open 24 hours.
place.why: It is the clearest example anywhere of water infrastructure that pays a second dividend: supply, flood control and a public space in one asset.
